title: GRPO: Group Relative Policy Optimization
hook: GRPO dropped the value network from PPO and scored each answer against a group of sampled siblings — the cheap RL recipe that made DeepSeek-R1's reasoning trainable.
key_points: Introduced in the DeepSeekMath paper as a leaner alternative to PPO for LLMs.
Removes PPO's separate value/critic model, roughly halving training memory.
Samples a group of answers per prompt and uses their mean reward as the baseline.
Became the workhorse RL algorithm behind DeepSeek-R1-style reasoning training.
content_html: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), introduced in the DeepSeekMath paper, is a reinforcement-learning method for fine-tuning language models that strips out the most expensive part of PPO. Instead of training a separate value network to estimate how good a state is, it estimates the baseline directly from a group of answers the model samples for the same prompt.
extra_html:
How it works

For each prompt, the model generates a group of candidate answers, each scored by a reward model. GRPO uses the group's average reward as the baseline, so an answer is reinforced in proportion to how much better (or worse) it is than its siblings. Because there is no critic network to train and store, GRPO uses substantially less memory and compute than PPO, while keeping the stability benefits of a relative advantage.

Why it matters

GRPO is the RL engine that made large-scale reasoning training affordable. DeepSeek used it to turn base models into strong reasoners (the R1 line) by rewarding correct, well-structured chains of thought. Its efficiency lowered the barrier for others to run reasoning-style RL, and "GRPO" quickly became shorthand for the post-PPO generation of preference and reasoning optimization.

related.title: PPO: Proximal Policy Optimization
related.hook: Reinforcement learning is notoriously unstable. PPO's fix is simple: never let a single update move the policy too far. That restraint made it the field's workhorse.

related.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
related.hook: DeepSeek shows strong reasoning can emerge from RL on verifiable rewards with minimal supervised data - and those reasoning traces can be distilled into smaller models.

related.title: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
related.hook: RLHF works but is fiddly: a separate reward model and a finicky RL loop. DPO reaches the same goal with one simple loss — and became a popular default.
